transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-23
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Rivers (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Auriga Head of ML), David Müller (Auriga Cloud Ops), Ana Costa (VP Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Auriga wants to renew current commitment and add a Dedicated pool in EU plus an on-prem pilot for sensitive workloads.
- Key asks: KMS/HSM integration, audit logs retention, latency SLOs for 2x peak traffic, proofs of performance for quantized variants.
- Next steps: SOW, security docs, benchmark plan, schedule pilot planning week of 7/6.

Topics: renewal timing, capacity uplift, EU on-prem pilot scope, encryption/KMS, SLA/latency, cost tradeoffs (batching/quant), rollout plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, um — hey everyone thanks for joining. we uh we scheduled 45, 50 minutes I think. quick check-in to make sure renewal alignment and the on-prem pilot scope, so why don't we do quick intros.
[00:12] Sara Patel: Sara Patel, Head of ML at Auriga. thanks Maya. I've got David and Ana with me.
[00:17] David Müller: David here, cloud ops. hi.
[00:19] Ana Costa: Ana, VP Engineering. good to see you.
[00:22] Liam Rivers: Liam Rivers, I'm a solutions engineer on the account — I'll drive the technical bits today.
[00:27] Maya Chen: Awesome. quick recap from us — you're coming up on renewal in August, right? and you mentioned wanting to add EU-dedicated nodes and an on-prem pilot for PHI-ish models. is that still the ask?
[00:38] Sara Patel: Yeah, correct. timeline's flexible but ideally we want contracts amended before end of July so procurement can sign. and, um, we want to run a small on-prem pilot for the models that touch regulated datasets.
[00:49] Ana Costa: Correct. we also want the dedicated capacity for predictable latency during our morning peaks in EU time zone.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Perfect. can you quickly remind us of current qps and latency targets during peak?
[01:00] David Müller: so right now baseline is about 120 rps across our global endpoints, EU peaks at roughly 45 rps sustained for 20 minutes, spiking to 80 for short bursts. latency target is 95th percentile under 180 ms for the short prompts we send.
[01:18] Liam Rivers: okay that's helpful. so two levers: Dedicated pool for throughput predictability, and for on-prem pilot we can do the private control plane option. quick note: our on-prem package does require some infra prerequisites — kubernetes cluster for the runtime, a permitted HSM or KMS endpoint, and connectivity to Redwood's control plane (or air-gapped variant if needed).
[01:41] Sara Patel: The air-gapped option is interesting but procurement is worried about extra ops. we likely want VPC/peered option first; on-prem might be in a sealed data center.
[01:50] Ana Costa: yeah, we prefer minimal ops hit. what's the typical lift for the private control plane? we had an earlier chat but need details for SRE estimates.
[01:57] Liam Rivers: Rough ballpark: for the private control plane, the install is around 3-5 days of engineer time for the initial deployment, plus a week of integration work for KMS and monitoring. that's assuming the infra meets spec. if you want a fully air-gapped on-prem then that's more — extra days for shipping artifacts and offline installers.
[02:14] Maya Chen: and to be clear on compliance — we have SOC2 artifacts and ISO certs. we'll share them in the packet. you'll need our KMS integration doc for the specific HSM vendor?
[02:24] Sara Patel: Yes please share — we use an HSM from SafeKey and a cloud KMS from Azura for backups. we need details on how Redwood handles key rotation, and whether keys can be customer-managed only.
[02:36] Liam Rivers: we support customer-managed keys; the POC we usually run uses an external KMS integration. key rotation is supported and logs are emitted to the audit stream; we'll send the KMS runbook.
[02:45] David Müller: audit logs retention — what's the retention default and can we push to our SIEM?
[02:50] Liam Rivers: default is 90 days in the console; enterprise add-on can extend retention longer. and yes, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. we'll include the specifics.
[02:58] Sara Patel: okay good. on the performance side, we need evidence that the quantized model variants won't regress on quality for our NLU tasks. we run a sensitive slot filling eval; if quality dips more than 2% F1 we can't use that variant.
[03:11] Liam Rivers: Understood. for that we usually run a small benchmark with your eval set — we can run the same prompt set across fp16 and 4-bit quant variants and show delta. availability of a quick regression alert in Optimize is possible too.
[03:23] Maya Chen: this is where Liam will prep the benchmark checklist. Liam can you outline what data we'll need from Auriga?
[03:28] Liam Rivers: Sure — we'll need: a sample prompt set (your eval), sample payload size distribution, expected token lengths, and frequency of streaming calls vs synchronous. also details on any tool-calling patterns.
[03:39] David Müller: we can pull that. question on cost: if we move to Dedicated EU, is burst capacity automatic or do we need to provision separate burst pools?
[03:47] Maya Chen: good question. Dedicated has reserved base and you can configure burst capacity via a burst pool option — costs are tracked separately; we'll include pricing tiers in the SOW. for critical windows we can reserve additional capacity.
[03:58] Ana Costa: what's the latency difference between hosted and Dedicated for EU region — typically?
[04:03] Liam Rivers: For a EU-dedicated pool, if the model is collocated in the same region, median latency is often 20–40 ms lower vs cross-region hosted. end-to-end numbers depend on network hops; so 95p could improve from 180ms to ~120–140ms in many configs.
[04:20] Sara Patel: good. one more compliance ask — our security team wants pen test results or at least the third-party assessment for the on-prem runtime. do you have artifacts?
[04:30] Liam Rivers: yes, we have third-party penetration test reports and hardened runtime checklists; we'll share them but can redact sensitive parts.
[04:36] Maya Chen: ok, quick planning — procurement wants a clear price for a 12-month renewal with a 3-month pilot window. ideally we present an SOW that shows the uplift cost for Dedicated EU and the on-prem pilot add-on.
[04:49] Sara Patel: timeline: procurement review by July 15, legal sign-off by July 28 latest. if you could get the SOW + security packet by June 25 that gives us time.
[04:58] Maya Chen: we can do that. action item — I'll send the draft SOW and pricing by Thursday (June 25).
[05:03] Liam Rivers: I'll own the benchmark checklist and a sample runbook for the on-prem install — will get that by next Monday (June 29).
[05:10] David Müller: I'll share our infra diagram and token length profile by Saturday (June 27).
[05:14] Ana Costa: one operational question: how does rollback work if we do a canary rollout when migrating traffic to Dedicated?
[05:22] Liam Rivers: rollouts are at the routing layer; you can do canary by % traffic, Redwood Console supports A/B and automatic fallback policies. if latency or error rate exceeds threshold, we auto-fallback to the previous model or to hosted variant.
[05:36] Sara Patel: any SLA delta for on-prem vs hosted?
[05:40] Maya Chen: Hosted has our standard SLA. On-prem/Private has a different operational model — we can contract for an SLA on the control plane connectivity and a response SLA for support but the underlying infra SLA is in your control. we'll call that out in the SOW.
[05:54] David Müller: noted. another question: do you support HSM-backed key wrapping in the private control plane?
[05:59] Liam Rivers: yes; the integration supports external HSMs and key wrapping. for air-gapped we do a certificate/key exchange procedure. we'll include the tech notes.
[06:10] [PAUSE - 10 seconds chatter about lunch]
[06:22] Maya Chen: okay, moving on to benchmarking specifics — Liam can you walk through the steps you'll run during the pilot?
[06:27] Liam Rivers: Absolutely. Step 1: baseline run against your hosted setup with the eval set. Step 2: run on Dedicated EU collocated model, measuring p50/p95 latency and token costs. Step 3: run quantized variants in a test harness to measure quality delta. Step 4: run on-prem runtime with same load to validate infra pattern. we'll produce a single report and a runbook of any infra tweaks.
[06:48] Sara Patel: will the on-prem run include KV cache behavior? we rely on prefix caching for sessions.
[06:54] Liam Rivers: yes, we'll validate KV cache warmup and cold-start latencies, and outline cache sizing recommendations.
[07:01] Ana Costa: and rolling upgrades — if we update model weights, what's the expected downtime?
[07:06] Liam Rivers: rolling upgrades are seamless in most configs — it's a staged rollout to nodes. for large model swaps we recommend warmup traffic and a short maintenance window; downtime should be negligible for inference, assuming cache strategies are pre-warmed.
[07:20] Maya Chen: there's a question from procurement that sometimes crops up — is there an early termination penalty if they take Dedicated for 12 months and then downsize?
[07:30] Maya Chen (continues): just want to flag so we can surface in SOW.
[07:33] Sara Patel: yes need clarity on that.
[07:35] Maya Chen: Typically dedicated commitments have a prorated termination clause; we'll include the terms in the SOW but it's standard to have a minimum notice and prorated fees for the remainder of the term.
[07:47] David Müller: good enough. small nit: do you have preferred network egress pattern for on-prem if we want to keep traffic internal?
[07:55] Liam Rivers: we support peering and private link; many customers use internal peering so egress is minimized. for air-gapped there's a local-only inference path.
[08:05] Sara Patel: wondering about cost optimization — we want Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, but also a clear estimate of token economics if we move 30% of traffic to quantized variants.
[08:15] Liam Rivers: we can model that — Optimize will run historical suggestions but for the pilot we'll produce a cost delta table.
[08:22] Maya Chen: ok let's talk dates — we commit to draft SOW by 6/25, security packet same day, Liam benchmark checklist by 6/29, infra diagram by 6/27. then a kickoff for the pilot week of 7/6 — does that align?
[08:34] Sara Patel: yes, that works for internal stakeholders.
[08:38] David Müller: agree.
[08:40] Ana Costa: yes.
[08:41] Maya Chen: Great. anything else?
[08:43] [small silence, faint keyboard sounds]
[09:00] Sara Patel: one more — can you confirm the model catalog: are you planning to keep the same model family or will you recommend a different architecture for on-prem? we saw some notes about kernel selection and quant friendliness.
[09:12] Liam Rivers: we'll recommend model variants based on your latency and quality targets; sometimes a slightly smaller architecture with 4-bit quant gives equal quality for specific NLU tasks but much lower cost. we'll include recommended models in the SOW.
[09:25] Maya Chen: also calling out that for the on-prem pilot we will provide a 'run to completion' checklist — like infra, network, certs, KMS, and a small acceptance test suite.
[09:35] David Müller: acceptance test pass/fail criteria — can we set them? for example 95 p95 under 180ms and <2% quality delta.
[09:43] Liam Rivers: absolutely. we'll formalize acceptance criteria in the SOW and in the benchmark report.
[09:49] Sara Patel: perfect. ok, I think that's all from our side.
[09:53] Maya Chen: cool. recap of next steps then — SOW + pricing + security packet by 6/25, infra diagram and token profile by 6/27, benchmark checklist by 6/29, pilot kickoff week of 7/6.
[10:06] Ana Costa: thanks Maya, Liam.
[10:08] Maya Chen: Thanks team. we'll follow up in email with links to the docs.

[10:20] NOTE: occasional transcription noise; names sometimes garbled (e.g., HSM vendor transcribed as SafeKey, might be SafeKay in internal recordings).
[10:30] End of meeting (approx 47 minutes).
